root_cause.text: The work item is cancelled before interrupts are disabled, creating a race where the interrupt handler can reschedule the work after cancellation but before freeing the IRQ, leading to use-after-free when the work accesses freed resources.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `cancel_work_sync(&ms->work)` after `free_irq(ms->irq0, ms)` and `free_irq(ms->irq1, ms)`, ensuring interrupts are disabled before cancelling work so no new work can be queued after cancellation. The commit message states: "The state machine work is scheduled by the interrupt handler and therefore needs to be cancelled after disabling interrupts to avoid a potential use-after-free."
